claims.claim: Emotions involve experience, appraisals, bodily responses and action tendencies, and people differ in how they label them. A racing heart can occur with excitement, fear, exertion or other causes; it is not proof of a particular emotion. A label is a tentative description, not a diagnosis. Research on affect labelling has investigated responses to emotional stimuli, but laboratory findings do not guarantee that naming an emotion will resolve distress. Practise descriptive vocabulary and allow uncertainty.

locators.limitations: Laboratory neural responses do not guarantee relief
